intent: Bars and a line on one chart over the same categories, like revenue as bars with growth rate as a line. One shared value axis, or a second axis on the right for the line.
useWhen: An amount and a rate or average over the same periods, like revenue with month-over-month growth
Volumes with a running target or moving average drawn across them
Two measures people read together per column, where two separate charts would make them line up by eye
Gains and losses per period with the net as a line — stack stacked, losses as negative values
doNotUseWhen: Only amounts compared across categories — use BarChart
Only a trend over time, one or several series — use LineChart
Part of a whole — use PieChart
A short ranking by one measure — use BarList

label.note: The category on the x axis, like Jan.

[key].note: One number per series key named in bars and line. A missing value draws no bar and breaks nothing: the line skips straight to the next point.

data.note: One row per category, in the order shown.

key.note: The data field this series reads.

label.note: Shown in the legend, the tooltip and the table.

bars.note: One to four bar series. They take --chart-1, --chart-2, --chart-4 and --chart-5 in order, so the line colour stays apart.

line.note: One line series, drawn smooth in --chart-3 with no area fill.

axis.note: shared puts bars and line on one left axis, for the same unit. dual gives the line its own axis on the right, for a different unit like a percent; its ticks line up with the left gridlines.

stack.note: stacked draws one bar per column: positive values pile up from zero and negative values pile down, in series order, with a hairline (surface.card) between segments. Use it for movements that add up, like gains and losses in a period, with the line as the net.

bars.note: (value: number) => string for bar values and the left axis.

line.note: (value: number) => string for line values and, with axis dual, the right axis.

valueFormatter.note: Both default to the chart format: 1,240, 12.4k, 1.2M. With axis shared, the left axis uses the bars formatter.

title.note: Chart heading on the frame, like the other charts. Also names the plot for screen readers.

actions.note: Kit Buttons in the chart header, before the Table toggle, like an icon-only Ask. ghost sm reads quietest. Setting it draws the frame even with no title.

requirements: Title on the figure when provided, and the plot is a role=group named by it
Each column is one focus stop in order; Tab and the arrow keys move column by column, and each column names its label and every bar and line value
The tooltip shows on focus as well as on hover, with every series for that column
The legend names each bar series and the line, with the line drawn as a line
The Table toggle swaps the chart for a plain table with every value

doNot: Do not use it for bars alone — use BarChart
Do not use it for lines alone — use LineChart
Do not stack a BarChart and a LineChart on top of each other to fake one — use ComboChart
Do not draw more than one line; a second trend belongs in LineChart
Do not use axis dual for values in the same unit; it makes the two scales look comparable when they are not
Do not use status colours for the series; a series that means good or bad says so in its label
Do not use raw hex or primitive --color-* ramps
Do not stack values that do not add up, like rates; use stack none
Do not pass losses as positive values with a status colour; make them negative so they pile below zero
Do not wrap a chart in a Card only to get a header button — pass actions
snippet:
<ComboChart
  title="Revenue and growth"
  description="2026, by month"
  axis="dual"
  data={[
    { label: "Jan", revenue: 42000, growth: 3.1 },
    { label: "Feb", revenue: 45500, growth: 8.3 },
    { label: "Mar", revenue: 44100, growth: -3.1 },
  ]}
  bars={[{ key: "revenue", label: "Revenue" }]}
  line={{ key: "growth", label: "Growth" }}
  valueFormatter={{ line: (value) => `${value}%` }}
/>

<ComboChart
  title="Seat changes"
  stack="stacked"
  data={[{ label: "Jan", added: 40, removed: -12, net: 28 }]}
  bars={[{ key: "added", label: "Added" }, { key: "removed", label: "Removed" }]}
  line={{ key: "net", label: "Net" }}
/>
